name: Wien's displacement law
meaning: Wavelength (micrometers) at which a blackbody at absolute temperature T (K) is brightest; 310 K gives about 9.3 micrometers, 5800 K about 500 nm.

name: Stefan-Boltzmann law
meaning: Total thermal power (W) radiated by a surface of area A (m^2), emissivity epsilon (0-1), and temperature T (K); sigma = 5.67e-8 W/(m^2 K^4).

name: Net radiative exchange
meaning: Net power (W) lost by an object at T to surroundings at T_s (both in K); positive means the object is cooling by radiation.

name: Thermal energy scale
meaning: Typical energy (J, or eV) of random motion per particle at temperature T; k_B = 1.381e-23 J/K, so about 0.026 eV at 300 K.

name: Photon energy from wavelength
meaning: Energy (eV) of a photon of wavelength lambda (nm); a 10 micrometer thermal-IR photon carries about 0.12 eV, matching molecular vibrations.
